subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — stakeholder map / procurement exception
messages:
From: Dana Li <dana.li@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@acme.com>
Date: 2027-02-10 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Intro + quick follow-up from this morning

Hi Marissa / Aditya,

Thanks for the intro call this morning — helpful overview. A quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can move toward procurement: 

- Purchase driver: customer-facing generative features for our knowledge base search; target is Q2 pilot for 5000 users.
- Key decision criteria: latency (<300ms for single-shot), cost per 1k predictions, model governance (audit logs + data residency), and vendor-managed SLAs.
- Stakeholders:
  - Product: Dana Li (me) — owner of the pilot
  - Eng: Carlos Ramirez — will validate perf and integration
  - Procurement: procurement@acme.com — will handle contract and security review
  - Legal: TBD

We have an internal procurement policy that usually requires three bids and standard SLA language; if Redwood can commit to a 99.9% inference availability SLA and provide SOC2 evidence + audit logs, we can fast-track. That said, I flagged the budget to Procurement and they asked whether any exceptions/discounts are possible if we commit to a 12-month reserved commit.

Next steps on our side: I can share an initial stakeholder map and loop Procurement. Can you share a proposed buying process timeline, an estimated TCO with and without reserved capacity, and any standard procurement redlines you see?

Thanks,
Dana

--
Dana Li
Director, Product @ Acme Corp
dana.li@acme.com

Subject: FW: Acme pilot — request for procurement/discount exception

Folks — forwarding Acme thread. Highlights:
- They are targeted for a Q2 pilot; decision drivers: latency, cost, SLA, audit logs.
- Procurement asked whether we can offer a discount for a 12-month reserved commit and whether we can move SLA to 99.9% for a Dedicated deployment.

I think this is a good candidate for a small procurement exception: 10% off list for a 12-month reserved commit + 99.9% SLA on Dedicated with a cap on credits. Connor — can you scope operational implications? Aditya — need TCO numbers and recommended discount range. Lauren — can you review for approval (procurement exception + SLA deviation)?

Attached: acme-stakeholder-map.xlsx (from the customer).

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise @ Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-11 15:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Acme pilot — request for procurement/discount exception

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the summary. I've reviewed the request and approve a procurement exception under the following conditions: 

1) Discount: up to 12% off list price for a 12-month reserved commit, provided we secure a minimum committed spend of $150k ARR.
2) SLA: approve a 99.9% inference availability SLA for Dedicated deployments only. Any SLA credits are capped at 10% of monthly committed spend and are subject to the standard incident review process.
3) Security/compliance: we will provide SOC 2 Type II report and audit log exports; any additional security evidence (pen test reports, if requested) will be treated as a paid add-on or requested via our SOC pack.
4) Legal redlines: no materially different indemnity or data residency clauses. Procurement must route redlines to Legal (legal@redwood.ai) — we won't accept open-ended liability without Legal signoff.

I am attaching the signed internal approval (procurement-exception-approval.pdf) and an updated pricing sheet (pricing-sheet-acme-v2.xlsx) with the approved discount. Please keep this thread for audit.

Approve: Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales Operations
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
